ACADEMY / Digital systems03 / 87
DIGITAL SYSTEMS03 / 87

The Internet is digital communication, not simply a website

People exchange messages, discover information, compare offers and respond. Digital systems can record selected events in that dialogue.

A digital market is a system of connected communication events. When captured lawfully and interpreted in context, these events become useful data.

A PERSON ASKS
A CHANNEL CONNECTS
A SIGNAL APPEARS
A DATA RECORD IS CREATED
A DECISION FOLLOWS

Before digitisation

A shop conversation might disappear when the customer leaves. The business remembers little unless someone records it.

After digitisation

A consenting visitor can leave a measurable trail: source, landing page, viewed category, contact request, order and feedback.
KEY PRINCIPLEThe Internet is a dynamic of communication and data. Data are meaningful only when interpreted in context.

ACADEMY / Digital systems04 / 87
DIGITAL SYSTEMS04 / 87

One customer journey generates connected evidence

Explore how a single message can produce data throughout the business.

SearchContentLeadPurchaseDeliveryExperience

Search signal

A visitor searches for a category or problem. Data: query theme and permitted referral. Decision: what topic matters?

Functional owner: CMO

What is first-party data?

Information a company obtains directly through its own customer relationships and channels, subject to appropriate privacy conditions.

Why connect signals?

An isolated click may indicate curiosity. A consented sequence of actions can help understand intent, conversion and service quality.

ACADEMY / Digital systems05 / 87
DIGITAL SYSTEMS05 / 87

Digitalisation creates a data system—not a data warehouse of everything

Capture only what is needed, make it reliable, and make it usable.

Data activation

Make recorded facts usable: define a customer ID, validate fields, join permitted records, trigger the right action and measure the outcome.

Internet dynamics

Read, capture, interpret and activate signals from search, digital communities, channels and the wider Internet environment—not simply connectivity.
DATA SOURCE
STRUCTURED INFORMATION
INTERPRETATION / AI
ACTION
EVIDENCE / LEARNING
KEY PRINCIPLEDigitalisation is implemented by CTO across the whole operating system. The CMO measures digital communication through POES channels using CPM, CTR, CPL and CPA. Official KAI·ROI ψᵢ remains the average of DataActivationᵢ and I_netᵢ.
WHO DOES WHAT?

CTO builds and maintains the digital platforms, integration, AI agents and access controls, funded through the approved transformation budget. CPIO audits data quality, provenance and responsible use. CMO uses a POES communication scorecard to measure whether those systems create market demand. Every area owns its data and its evidence.

Teaching proxy: POES channel performance is an operational diagnostic of digital communication—not a substitution for the official ψᵢ calculation.

CohortApproximate birth yearsContext to investigate—not a rule
Baby Boomers1946–1964Adoption history, channel trust and service expectations
Generation X1965–1980Hybrid analogue/digital experience, reliability and practicality
Millennials / Gen Y1981–1996Mobile and platform adoption, transparent value comparisons
Generation Z1997–2012Social discovery, rapid content formats, peer signals

Sustainable Development Goals: impact must be tangible

The UN has 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Companies should identify material goals and measure relevant impacts.

People

  • SDG 3 · Good Health and Well-being
  • SDG 4 · Quality Education
  • SDG 5 · Gender Equality
  • SDG 8 · Decent Work and Economic Growth

Planet

  • SDG 12 · Responsible Consumption and Production
  • SDG 13 · Climate Action
  • SDG 6 · Clean Water and Sanitation
  • SDG 7 · Affordable and Clean Energy

Prosperity & institutions

  • SDG 9 · Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure
  • SDG 10 · Reduced Inequalities
  • SDG 16 · Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
  • SDG 17 · Partnerships for the Goals

What CPIO measures

  • A material impact objective
  • Baseline and measurable unit
  • Evidence source, owner and reporting period
  • Unintended adverse effects

These examples introduce selected SDGs, not the full list. Official framework: UN 2030 Agenda / 17 SDGs.

Rules / classical AIMachine learningDeep learningGenerative AIAI workflowsCo-pilotsAgentic AI

Rules / classical AI

ACADEMY / People & AI09 / 87
PEOPLE & AI09 / 87

AI as a co-worker: assistance, boundaries and accountability

Automation does not remove the need for people to own decisions.

Human responsibility

People decide objectives, approve consequential actions, understand customer context, review exceptions and remain accountable.

AI contribution

Assist with drafting, extraction, classification, data checking, retrieval, forecasting and monitored workflow execution.

Safety gate

  • Lawful and minimal data
  • Human sign-off on consequential decisions
  • Traceable sources and changes
  • Tests for bias, errors and security

Value gate

  • Quality before speed
  • Hours released vs cash savings
  • Support and upskilling for colleagues
  • Measure customer benefit and economic efficiency

ACADEMY / Ethics & identity10 / 87
ETHICS & IDENTITY10 / 87

The DEEP ethical code: respect comes first

Ethics is a management specification, not a decorative statement.

PRIMARY SOURCEEasy Deep / Kukulcan AI Consulting · Code of Ethics for the Application of AI (uploaded PDF, pp. 2–6).Download the original DEEP ethical code (PDF)Source notes →

Respect & human oversight

Respect people, data and cultural contexts. Keep humans in control of critical decisions.

Transparency

Explain where AI is used, document limitations and make decisions auditable.

Context

Do not apply the same model blindly across languages, groups or markets.

Purposeful data

Collect only what is necessary; define purpose, quality and retention limits.
KEY PRINCIPLEA business should define ethical boundaries before it decides how to collect data or automate customer contact.

ACADEMY / Ethics & identity11 / 87
ETHICS & IDENTITY11 / 87

The DEEP code: knowledge, intellectual property and responsible growth

The second half of the code explains how a company can share knowledge and deploy agents without losing control.

Responsible sharing

Use defined communities, agreements, secure access and traceability; balance openness and confidentiality.

Intellectual property

Respect authorship, methods, designs and licensing; review the provenance of input data and outputs.

Tokens & NFTs

The code discusses tokens as potential traceability tools; they do not replace legal intellectual-property rights.

Agent governance

Define what agents may do, test outputs, document exceptions and provide human-supervised control.

Data guardians

Assign data stewards, risk officers or an ethics board appropriate to the organisation.

Dignified efficiency

Use time released by AI to improve meaningful work, support teams and build sustainable value—not as a justification for dismissals.

This educational summary reflects the uploaded DEEP code. It is not independent legal advice or a substitute for the source document.

ACADEMY / Innovation & market13 / 87
INNOVATION & MARKET13 / 87

Mission starts with an innovation you can actually sell

Move from a real problem to an identifiable product, not a vague aspiration.

Innovation

What is different or meaningfully improved? Test customer needs, feasibility, value, cost and evidence.

Mission · practical classroom framing

Specify what we create and sell, for whom, why it matters, what distinguishes it and at what price.

Vision · practical classroom framing

Describe the future market position and target customer identity we aspire to serve. This is a proposed operating interpretation, not the only accepted academic definition.

Business promise

What the buyer receives, what the company can deliver, what it costs and what proof supports the offer.
KEY PRINCIPLE“We empower consumers” is not enough. “We sell a specified product at a tested price to a defined customer” can guide decisions.

Methods that turn innovation into a marketable product

Research first, test quickly, learn from evidence and improve what the customer receives.

MethodPlain-English questionPractical output
Design ThinkingWhat problem are we really solving?Customer insight and prototype
Jobs to Be DoneWhat progress is the customer trying to make?Functional, social and emotional job
Lean StartupWhich risky assumption should we test first?Minimum viable test and learning
Business Model CanvasHow can this business create and capture value?Business model hypothesis
Value Proposition CanvasWhy should this customer choose us?Fit of pains, gains and offer

Methodologies are complementary, not interchangeable. A sprint is a short execution and learning interval; an 18-month strategy is a longer governance horizon.

ACADEMY / Innovation & market15 / 87
INNOVATION & MARKET15 / 87

Product specification: make the offer tangible

Students must be able to describe the precise product—not merely a category.

01
Identify the SKU or service

Name, edition, size, quantity, physical or digital configuration.

02
State verifiable attributes

Materials, ingredients, origin, quality, access conditions and supporting evidence.

03
Translate features into customer benefits

Explain the use case and the advantage without unsupported claims.

04
Specify customer terms

Price, applicable taxes, delivery, returns, guarantee, support and SLA.

05
Confirm supply and capacity

Stock, producer commitments, staff hours or service slots and release criteria.

Product example · teaching scenario

Don Espadín · premium mezcal “Foundational Edition” · one 700 mL bottle (illustrative specification to be verified) · retail price €99.99 incl. 21% VAT.

Services work the same way

A consultancy package has an SKU-like service definition: scope, deliverables, expert hours, availability, price, acceptance criteria and SLA.

The uploaded economic scenario provides the €99.99 price. Bottle volume and other attributes shown here are working assumptions requiring verification.

Follow one sale from the consumer price to the economic contribution.

What the CFO checks

  • Correct VAT rate and tax treatment
  • Any excise duties, fees and import conditions
  • Direct and shared cost allocation
  • Whether revenue is earned, collected or deferred

  • Production, materials and supplier terms
  • Capacity, inventory, fulfilment and returns

ACADEMY / Innovation & market17 / 87
INNOVATION & MARKET17 / 87

Vision becomes a customer identity worth testing

Define whose future needs the offer is designed to serve, then verify them with research.

Buyer Persona: evidence-based hypothesis

  • Context and buying occasion
  • Needs, pains and desired outcomes
  • Decision criteria, objections and alternatives
  • Search terms, channels and trusted sources
  • Budget and buying frequency

Example hypothesis · Don Espadín

  • Urban premium-oriented adult, approx. 46–61
  • Gifting, hosting and ritual as occasions
  • Needs verifiable provenance and product detail
  • Concerns: price, authenticity, shipping and unknown brand
  • Validation: interviews, conversion and service feedback
KEY PRINCIPLEA buyer persona is not a fictional stereotype. It is a hypothesis that becomes useful when customer evidence confirms or corrects it.

C-LEVEL ORGANISATION19 / 87

What is a CEO? What does C-Level mean?

Every business needs responsibilities even when it has only one or two people.

CEO — Chief Executive Officer

The chief executive who makes the final strategic choices, approves the planning horizon, sets priorities and asks leaders to provide evidence.

C-Level

Senior functional responsibility (chief executive roles). A role is a duty, not necessarily a different employee.

Process owner

The person accountable for making a process work, collecting evidence and managing exceptions.

KPI owner

The person responsible for the definition, quality and explanation of a specific measure.
KEY PRINCIPLEOne business, many responsibilities. A small company may combine roles without losing the need to assign ownership.

ACADEMY / C-Level organisation21 / 87
C-LEVEL ORGANISATION21 / 87

CEO: approval of the 19-month value-creation programme

The CEO decides where the company is going and when the management cycle begins.

01
Understand the market

Consider people, ethics, customer demand, competitors, technology and impact.

02
Approve the offer

Select the innovation, market, product, acceptable price and positioning.

03
Approve ambitions and constraints

Agree financial targets, customer quality, capacity, brand guardrails, budget and risk limits.

04
Start the cycle

Month 0 prepares the baseline, evidence, owners and roadmap; months 1–18 execute.

05
Decide every 15 days

Review evidence, remove blockers and formally authorise relevant adjustments.

KEY PRINCIPLEThe CEO owns strategic decisions; other executives own the operational evidence that makes those decisions executable.

ACADEMY / C-Level organisation22 / 87
C-LEVEL ORGANISATION22 / 87

CPO: ABC is a prioritisation method, not a person

The procurement role secures the right products or service hours at the right time and under the right conditions.

ABC classification, step by step

01
List items

Record every SKU or service category and its demand.

02
Choose an approved value criterion

For example annual consumption value = units × unit cost.

03
Rank and calculate cumulative share

Sort highest first; compute each item’s share of total value.

04
Group A / B / C

Illustratively A ≈ 80% of value, B ≈ 15%, C ≈ 5%—thresholds are policy choices, not universal truths.

What the CPO does afterwards

  • Check forecast from demand and customer prioritisation
  • Contract producers and SLA terms
  • Release purchase orders and secure stock or booked hours
  • Update availability, quality and ABCD records
  • Handover capacity and accepted items to the COO
IMPORTANTClassic ABC inventory analysis is a teaching method. ABCDᵢ is also a formal component of SPOᵢ; its precise semantic definition is not replaced here by a generic ABC method.

Procurement separation: CPO buys SKUs and physical marketing merchandise. CHRO manages all FTE/hour-based service contracts. A request from Marketing can therefore produce a CPO SKU purchase order or a CHRO FTE SLA, never an ambiguous single contract.

ACADEMY / C-Level organisation27 / 87
C-LEVEL ORGANISATION27 / 87

CFO Control: costs, cash, WACC and economic discipline

The finance function protects the budget, manages funding and makes the economic result comparable.

OPEX and CAPEX

OPEX is operating expenditure. CAPEX is capital investment; it is typically recognised on the balance sheet and expensed over time through depreciation or amortisation where applicable.

WACC

Weighted Average Cost of Capital: the blended cost of financing from equity and debt. It is not a general tax rate or an arbitrary penalty.

Cash vs income

Customers may pay before revenue is earned, and suppliers may be paid after costs arise. Deposits and loyalty obligations require appropriate accounting.

Control evidence

Approved budgets, supplier invoices, payment schedule, cost standards, financial close, funding assumptions and exceptions.
KEY PRINCIPLECFO checks how value is financed and what it costs. Without this, “higher sales” can hide poor cash economics.

CXO: NPS, RFM, LTV, churn and the customer portfolio

Customer value continues after delivery. Experience determines whether the relationship grows.

NPS — recommendation likelihood

Ask a 0–10 recommendation question. Promoters score 9–10, passives 7–8 and detractors 0–6. NPS = % promoters − % detractors (range −100 to +100).

Dynamic RFM

Recency = how recently someone purchased; Frequency = how often; Monetary = economic purchasing value. Weighted and time-aware RFM can feed Cognitive Category CCᵢ.

LTV — Lifetime Value

Estimated value from a customer relationship over a defined horizon, using an approved revenue/margin definition and assumptions.

Churn & Retention

Churn = customers lost from a defined cohort during a defined period. Retention = 1 − churn. Absence from a website alone is not proof of churn.
PORTFOLIO HEALTH · OFFICIAL OPERATIONAL DEVELOPMENTΓ_g(i),t = √[(LTV_g,t / LTV_g,0) × (Retention_g,t / Retention_g,0)]. The formal position of Γ in KAI is preserved.

The marketplace has two stories: the customer and the organisation

MARKETPLACE ARCHITECTURE & SYSTEMS35 / 87

The systems glossary: CRM, CMS, POS, ERP, WHS and BI

Acronyms are not business outcomes. Each system exists to make a specific process reliable.

CRM · Customer Relationship Management

Manages customer relationships, history, qualified leads, loyalty and service interactions.

CMS · Content Management System

Publishes and manages content. Not a substitute for identity, payment or stock management.

POS · Point of Sale

Captures sales at the point of commercial interaction and produces transaction evidence.

ERP · Enterprise Resource Planning

Connects purchasing, finance, stock, service capacity and enterprise records.

WHS / WMS · Warehouse System

Manages physical goods, locations, work, picking, packing and fulfilment evidence.

BI · Business Intelligence

Consolidates consistent metrics for accountable analysis and executive decision-making.

All systems share identifiers and explicit data contracts. A screen is an interface; an authenticated action is an event; a validated event becomes evidence.

The complete process is a sequence of governed handoffs

Do not ask students to memorise eleven acronyms before seeing why they must collaborate.

CEO→CPO→CMO→CRO→CFO-R→COO→CFO-W→CXO→CPIO→CHRO→CTO

Top-down: CEO mandate

Direction sets the product, price, ethical boundaries, customer hypothesis, financial capacity and targets. The authorised programme runs one preparation month plus eighteen execution months.

Bottom-up: customer evidence

Every permitted event generates a verifiable record. Data, task time, service quality and economics return to the committee for further decisions.

The process does not operate as eleven departments waiting in line. CTO, CHRO and CPIO must safeguard technology, people and data quality from the first transaction.

Two procurements, two accountable owners

CPO · Physical SKUs

Product units, packaging, printed media merchandise, stored stock, quality acceptance, purchase orders and goods suppliers' SLAs.

CHRO · FTE service capacity

Agency hours, salespeople, warehouse teams, drivers and delivery staff. CHRO owns FTE SLAs and SLAd; requesters own their task requirements.

Financial control: CFO-W verifies purchase commitments, budget availability and payment orders, while CPIO checks data and quality evidence.

CENTRAL RULE · CHRO OWNS EVERY FTE-BASED SLA

All people-capacity SLAs belong to CHRO regardless of the requesting function. This includes CMO marketing and POES agency hours; CRO commercial or contact-centre hours; COO warehouse operators, route staff and drivers (SLAd); and specialist hours requested by other executive functions.

The requesting executive defines scope, deliverables, required hours, standards, acceptance criteria and budget owner. CHRO sources capacity, arranges contracts, records the hour-based SLA, maintains the task inventory and measures P × Q, training needs and learning-by-doing improvements. CFO-W authorises spending and payment. CTO enables workforce tools; CPIO checks data and quality evidence.

Functional request → CHRO workforce plan → supplier / worker capacity and SLA → performance P × Q → learning and development → management decision.

FTE means full-time equivalent, a capacity measure; working hours, not headcount reduction, are the planning unit. Released time should support people and sustainable value creation.

A customer order: trace every decision from message to Customer Equity

One business event can cross many departments without losing its identity, consent or evidence.

01 · CEO

02 · CPO

Confirm inventory / FTS capacity and approved supplier commitments.

Capture lawful campaign engagement and hand a qualified MQL to Sales.

Convert an SQL into a confirmed transaction and complete customer order details.

05 · CFO-R

Number the order; decide payment or credit release; account for revenue and taxes.

06 · COO

Pick, pack, route, deliver and record signed proof plus hours and SLA.

07 · CFO-W

Reconcile cost, supplier payments, cash, capital and financial reports.

08 · CXO

Activate member experience, handle incidents, record NPS and retention signals.

09 · CPIO · CHRO · CTO

Audit evidence, improve work with dignity, govern systems/AI and inform the CEO.

Example boundary: Don Espadín price €99.99 including VAT is a working case assumption, not proof of an order or profitability. A real output requires observed quantities, valid fiscal records, costs and checked delivery evidence.

How the spiral becomes a real 19-month programme

Month 0 authorises the system; months 1–18 produce traceable evidence and new decisions.

1Preparation month (M0)
18Execution months (M1–M18)
15Days between committee reviews
11Executive owners contributing evidence

Baseline = previous year

Each positive, comparable performance metric starts from a baseline index of 1. A target of 1.20 means an intended 20% improvement over that baseline; this does not by itself demonstrate a 20% ROI increase.

Two separate progress readings

Every fortnight compare actual performance with the prior-year baseline and with the scheduled objective. Keep direct income, verified efficiency, resource cost and customer economics apart.

Consolidation rule: the operating progress index may combine comparable, validated contributions for a teaching simulation; reported ROI and Customer Equity require their own financial and formal calculations.

The decision board: where evidence becomes accountability

Each executive gets five minutes, but must show source, target, result, explanation and next action.

01 · Target

What value did you promise for this review?

02 · Reality

What is the observed value, not an invented or missing zero?

03 · Comparison

How does actual performance compare with the prior-year baseline and current milestone?

04 · Explanation

Which tasks, cases or data explain the movement?

05 · Economic evidence

Where did real income, verified efficiency or cost move?

06 · Next decision

Which owner, resource, approval or correction is needed?

The board serves the CEO, but it is also a learning loop for every C-Level. The objective is not to display 50 disconnected dashboards: it is to build one defensible, client-centred explanation of organisational value.

Keep the official KAI·ROI equation separate from the new operating map

The 50-capability inventory and the 43-slot mapping help implement, observe and explain; they do not redefine the formal model.

Official sovereign structure:
KAIᵢ* = φᵢ · uᵢ · fᵢ · ψᵢ · SPOᵢ · Pᵢ · Γg(i),t
ψᵢ = average(DataActivationᵢ, I_netᵢ)
SPOᵢ = CCᵢ · ABCDᵢ · NPSᵢ
MDᵢ = Σs (Iᵢ,s · Rᵢ,s + Eᵢ,s · Qᵢ,s)
CEᵢ = (((KAIᵢ* · MDᵢ − Cᵢ) / Cᵢ) − WACCₜ) / WACCₜ
CE_company = Σi CEᵢ
V%CE = (100 / N) · Σi 1(CEᵢ > 0)

Operational ownership (not replacement)

CEO: Direction / Objectives. CPO: ABCD data. CMO: digital activation. CRO, COO, CHRO: productivity evidence. CFO-R: transactions and RFM. CXO: NPS, LTV and retention. CFO-W: financial consolidation. CPIO: audits. CTO: intelligence, systems, SPO governance.

Economic interpretation

MD explicitly records positive data-generated income/impact and verified efficiency. Costs belong in C. Γ measures LTV and retention relative to their starting values. An operational factor of 1 denotes baseline, not necessarily each formal factor.

Any proposed ROI × operating-index illustration must be labelled a simulation. It is neither the official CE formula nor proof of economic causality. Data unavailable ≠ 0.

01
Net revenue

Consumer price excluding VAT and adjustments × recognised sales volume.

02
Variable contribution

Net revenue − approved variable costs; clarify which costs the model includes.

03
EBITDA

Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation; deduct relevant operating expenses without double counting.

04
EBIT

EBITDA − depreciation − amortisation; CAPEX is not fully deducted in EBITDA when capitalised.

05
Profit before tax

EBIT − net finance costs (plus other applicable items).

06
Net profit

Profit before tax − applicable income tax, adjusted for tax losses and relevant accounting rules.

07
Cash & funding

Separately analyse collections, payments, CAPEX, working capital and financing cost / WACC.

08
Profit allocation policy

Only distributable profit can be allocated according to approved policies and applicable legal/accounting restrictions.

Illustrative policy proposed for discussion

  • 5% of distributable profit for an employee participation mechanism
  • 5% for reinvestment in research and development (R&D)
  • Remaining distributable amount for shareholders, if approved and legally permitted

Do not confuse

  • Corporate income tax ≠ VAT collected
  • CAPEX ≠ immediate operating expense
  • EBITDA ≠ cash
  • A 5% allocation ≠ an automatic legal entitlement
KEY PRINCIPLEPrice supports a business only if the financial structure, capacity and actual demand support it.

SWOT: diagnose the actual world before choosing objectives

Strengths and weaknesses describe internal factors. Opportunities and threats describe external conditions.

INTERNAL · POSITIVESTRENGTHS

What capabilities, data, supply or distinctive assets do we already have?

INTERNAL · NEGATIVEWEAKNESSES

What gaps in budget, skills, evidence or execution could prevent delivery?

EXTERNAL · POSITIVEOPPORTUNITIES

Which market shifts, needs, channels or partnerships could help?

EXTERNAL · NEGATIVETHREATS

Which competitors, regulations, supply shocks or changes in preference could hurt?

Operational diagnostic · φ_SWOT

POS = w_F·F + w_O·O; NEG = w_D·D + w_A·A; φ_SWOT = POS − NEG. Range −100 to +100. Zero means balanced diagnostic.

Official φᵢ

Direction / Decision remains the formal variable. A zero SWOT diagnostic cannot be inserted as a multiplicative formal factor. Any transformation requires explicit authorisation.

The Golden Sprint Spiral of executive responsibility

Your model: each turn makes the organisation return to Direction with more evidence and better decisions.

THE ORIGINAL GOLDEN SPRINT SPIRALSelect any blue executive label to explore its responsibilities, evidence and lesson.

CEO · Chief Executive Officer

Direction, product decision and organisational objectives

Approves the mission, product/market intent, initial price, strategic objectives, 19-month programme and accountability; validates conflicts and reallocations.

Evidence / handover: Decision log, approved strategic brief, objectives and budget.

What is a sprint?

A short execution and review interval with a defined owner, task backlog, evidence and decision. Multiple sprints fit inside the 18-month horizon.

What does the spiral mean?

The customer-value chain runs continuously. The CEO starts and reviews the cycle, while all executives work with shared evidence.

Data Monetisation (MD): income and economic efficiency

Management wants to see revenue and validated efficiency—not just clicks or an abstract score.

Income / economic impact

  • Attributable additional orders or income
  • Captured or realised economic benefit
  • Scenario, attribution and confidence checks
  • No double-counted customer revenue

Efficiency / operational improvement

  • Verified time or resource savings
  • Reduced operational losses or waste
  • Quality and implementation factor
  • Hours released are not automatically cash savings
OFFICIAL DATA MONETISATIONMDᵢ = Σₛ (Iᵢ,ₛ · Rᵢ,ₛ + Eᵢ,ₛ · Qᵢ,ₛ)

Costs associated with the scenarios belong in Cᵢ. Do not deduct them again in MDᵢ.

KEY PRINCIPLEKAI·ROI seeks measurable economic value while improving customers, productivity, dignity and the health of the portfolio.

Previous year = 1: the management baseline is not the target

Every C-Level defines a realistic improvement target and records evidence every 15 days.

KPIPrevious yearTargetBetter-direction rule
Qualified-lead volume100 leads = 1.00120 leads = 1.20Current / baseline
Cost per lead (CPL)€10 = 1.00€8 → 1.25Baseline / current
Orders per hour5 = 1.006 → 1.20Current / baseline
Customer retention80% = 1.0084% → 1.05Current / baseline

1.00

The previous-year result is preserved. A target of 1.20 means the goal is improvement—not merely equal performance.

Comparison rules

Only use positive comparable bases; handle negative, zero, cohort-dependent or signed indicators (e.g. NPS) with separately approved methods.

Operational improvement indices are not identical to official KAI factors or a causal economic attribution model.

Working persona

Urban premium consumer, approximately 46–61 years old, interested in hosting, gifting, discovery and ritual. Age is a targeting hypothesis to test, not a guarantee of behaviour.

Decision drivers

Trusted origin, 100% agave evidence, clear tasting descriptions, comparisons, genuine reviews, delivery reliability and gift presentation.

Objections

Digital evidence

Consented search intent, on-page content engagement, preferred value proposition, selected offer benefit, first-party identifiers and recorded order outcomes.

ACADEMY / APPLIED CASE · DON ESPADÍN80 / 87
CEO · SWOT → GOALS → BUDGET80 / 87

From SWOT to the financial commitments: a product cannot survive on narrative alone

Connect external conditions and internal capabilities to explicit volume, cost, price, investment and performance targets.

DON ESPADÍN · COURSE CASECEO · SWOT → GOALS → BUDGET

Premium Espadín mezcal · Spain / EU entry · simulated commercial and customer datasets

SWOT → initiatives

Assess a new premium brand's differentiation, limited recognition, premium purchase occasions and competitive alternatives; validate each SWOT statement before using it to allocate budgets.

Consumer price waterfall

€99.99 including 21% VAT → approximately €17.35 VAT → €82.64 net selling revenue per unit. Sales VAT is not the company's revenue.

Planning economics

Working illustration: role-owned budgets €54.43 per unit, contribution €28.21 per unit, fixed OPEX €120,000, target surplus €75,000; assumed unit sales scenario 11,000.

Viability gates

Illustrative break-even: 4,254 units; illustrative sustainable threshold including surplus target: 6,913 units. These rely on unchanged contribution assumptions—not observed profit.

€99.99Retail price · VAT incl.
€82.64Net revenue / unit
€28.21Illustrative contribution / unit
4,254Illustrative break-even · units
KEY PRINCIPLEObjectives and budget translate innovation into measurable commitments; actual cost data, CAPEX and cash timing remain independently verifiable.

ACADEMY / APPLIED CASE · DON ESPADÍN81 / 87
CPO · SKU / CHRO · FTE SLA81 / 87

Buy physical SKUs; contract professional hours through CHRO

CPO supplies the product and physical merchandising. CHRO contracts all FTE/time-based service capacity.

DON ESPADÍN · COURSE CASECPO · SKU / CHRO · FTE SLA

Premium Espadín mezcal · Spain / EU entry · simulated commercial and customer datasets

CPO / Procurement Compass

Use demand, approved product forecasts, supplier proposals, orders and ABCD records to source mezcal SKUs, packaging and physical campaign merchandise.

Warehouse and product availability

Document receiving, quality control, storage, picking readiness, packaging, stock rotation, returns and the SKU-specific supplier SLA.

CHRO / FTE service agreement

Procure and manage contracted hours for marketing agencies, sales personnel, warehouse operators, transport drivers and other professional services, using standard hours and agreed quality.

Evidence gates

An approved SKU order or an approved FTE SLA creates commitments; supplier confirmation, available capacity, proof of service and costs must travel to the operating and finance systems.

KEY PRINCIPLENever treat inventory supply and labour-hour capacity as the same procurement flow: they have distinct owners and evidence.

POES & campaign evidence

Paid, Owned, Earned and Shared channels generate impressions, clicks, leads and acquisitions. Compute CPM, CTR, CPL and CPA only when inputs are known.

Marketing → MQL

Tags (channel, UTM, message and offer), landing behaviour, legitimate lead consent, qualification rules and attribution events become a traceable MQL record.

Sales → SQL

Cross-channel teaching result

57 managed SQL opportunities → 38 won overall. The illustrative first-purchase flow has 25 MQL wins plus 15 direct e-commerce orders = 40 first purchasers.

ACADEMY / APPLIED CASE · DON ESPADÍN83 / 87
CFO-R → COO → CFO-W83 / 87

An accepted sale becomes an order, a delivery and an accountable financial result

Follow the order across systems without confusing revenue, credit, tax, cash, logistics or inventory cost.

DON ESPADÍN · COURSE CASECFO-R → COO → CFO-W

Premium Espadín mezcal · Spain / EU entry · simulated commercial and customer datasets

CFO Revenue / e-commerce

Approve credit where relevant, record net sales and VAT separately, capture the payment state, create the order number and update transactional history for RFM.

COO / warehouse and delivery

Receive the order; route it through picking, packing, dispatch, handoff and customer receipt. Track route, assigned driver/vehicle, elapsed time, proof of delivery and SLA exceptions.

Working shipping assumption

Distribution benchmark: €9.90 per order, subject to vehicle fill, geography and routing. Estimated marketing €10.50 and reserve €1.00 must not be added again if already part of a consolidated unit budget.

CFO Financial Control

Validate supplier payables, contracted FTE services, cash and credit commitments, working capital, WACC and costs; calculate financial results without recognising tax or deposits as earned revenue.

KEY PRINCIPLEThe order lifecycle must reconcile commercial events, warehouse actions, supplier obligations and the financial ledger.

ACADEMY / APPLIED CASE · DON ESPADÍN84 / 87
CXO → CPIO → CHRO → CTO84 / 87

After delivery: experience, portfolio health, quality, productivity and intelligence

The most valuable customer journey continues after the first transaction.

DON ESPADÍN · COURSE CASECXO → CPIO → CHRO → CTO

Premium Espadín mezcal · Spain / EU entry · simulated commercial and customer datasets

CXO / customer experience

Example master has 266 synthetic customer records; NPS exercise includes 160 survey responses. The NPS score itself is Unknown unless response distribution is loaded.

RFM, loyalty, LTV and retention

Track repeat transactions by recency, frequency and monetary value; use legitimate cohort data to estimate LTV, annual retention and churn; keep NPS, ABCD and cognitive category inputs distinct.

CPIO / DIIIP and quality

Audit data provenance, ETL, agent activity, system controls, ODS/SDG impact and the quality of evidence. Quality audits are not a replacement for the NPS or formal SPO factor.

CHRO and CTO

CHRO consolidates organisational productivity using task-based standards and quality, strengthening teams. CTO operates digital systems, AI tools and controlled SPO integration.

DATA QUALITY GATE266 synthetic customer IDs ≠ 266 verified active customers. 160 responses ≠ an NPS value. Churn and LTV remain unknown until cohort and purchase evidence is supplied.
KEY PRINCIPLEA one-time purchase is not proof of Customer Equity; portfolio health requires valid LTV and retention measurements.

ACADEMY / APPLIED CASE · DON ESPADÍN85 / 87
CEO · EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE · LEARNING SPIRAL85 / 87

The 19-month Golden Sprint: what an executive actually reviews every 15 days

Month 0 prepares the business. Months 1–18 execute the agreed plan and produce evidence for the next decision.

DON ESPADÍN · COURSE CASECEO · EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE · LEARNING SPIRAL

Premium Espadín mezcal · Spain / EU entry · simulated commercial and customer datasets

One month to prepare

Approve innovation and offer, ethical boundaries, brand and target segment, SWOT, economic objectives, budgets, process ownership, baseline KPIs, data contracts and resource capacity.

Eighteen months to execute

Follow initiative schedules, launch and supply capacity, campaigns, transactions, delivery and service improvements. Each executive owns traceable actions.

Previous year = 1

An operational performance index of 1 means no change from a comparable prior-year baseline; >1 improvement; <1 deterioration, oriented appropriately for cost KPIs.

Biweekly executive reviews

Each C-Level presents planned vs actual, evidence quality, deviation, attributed income/efficiency and next decisions. A combined index is not by itself proof of realised ROI.

KEY PRINCIPLEThe spiral is a learning metaphor; φ_i in formal KAI·ROI remains Direction / Decision, not the number 1.618 or a 19-month numeric constant.

ACADEMY / APPLIED CASE · DON ESPADÍN86 / 87
CLASSROOM · GROUP PROJECT · ASSESSMENT86 / 87

Your assessment: replicate Don Espadín in a business of your own

The final examination is a coherent evidence trail—not memorising acronyms or decorating a business plan.

DON ESPADÍN · COURSE CASECLASSROOM · GROUP PROJECT · ASSESSMENT

Premium Espadín mezcal · Spain / EU entry · simulated commercial and customer datasets

Deliverable 1 — Buyer Persona

Specify a legal, viable market segment, its context, needs, trust signals, objections and ethically capturable behavioural evidence.

Deliverable 2 — SWOT

Present a traceable internal/external diagnosis; prioritise and connect each finding to an initiative.

Deliverable 3 — Goals & Budget

Separate VAT from revenue; price the offer, justify capacity, OPEX/CAPEX, unit economics, targets and responsible financial assumptions.

Deliverables 4–5 — PDP and KPI Strategy Map

Build an evidence-backed product page and a 1+18-month monitoring plan with C-Level ownership, baseline, target, cadence and proof of handoffs.

CLASSROOM CHALLENGE · 40 MINUTES

Teams select their own product or service, map the 11 C-Level handoffs, identify five essential files and propose two objective KPIs. Afterwards, students continue individual deliverables using the recommended treatments.

KEY PRINCIPLELearners may reproduce the method with another company, compare cases or challenge the assumptions; factual evidence and ethical use take priority.

CLASSROOM PRACTICE87 / 87

Source notes, limits and original authorship

Transparency helps distinguish source evidence, classroom assumptions and protected formal architecture.

User-provided primary sources

  • Easy Deep / Kukulcan AI Consulting: Code of Ethics for the Application of AI, six-page PDF.
  • DOC_ROI_Goals_and_Budget (1).csv: cost ownership, unit assumptions and evidence gates.
  • DOC ROI SWOT Direction Builder: diagnostic structure and φ_SWOT operational methodology.
  • DOC ROI Objectives & Initiatives: SWOT input, CAME, required work, owners, portfolio, goals and budget.
  • The supplied executive spiral and economic planning images.
  • Don Espadín: five product/brand photographs, identity marks, working price and business scenario, and simulated CRM, NPS and sales-flow datasets supplied for educational use.

Conventions and limitations

  • KAI·ROI official v1 structure is reproduced without amendment.
  • 19 months = one preparation month plus 18 execution months.
  • Golden spiral = narrative metaphor, not a formally derived planning duration.
  • No unknown input is silently treated as zero.
  • Worked economic and ROI examples are demonstrations, not audited results.
ACADEMIC REFERENCE STARTING POINTSUN Sustainable Development Goals (2015); GDPR principles (EU); NIST AI Risk Management Framework (2023); OECD AI Principles; Lean Startup, Design Thinking and Jobs to Be Done foundational approaches. Check jurisdiction-specific requirements and current versions before professional use.
KEY PRINCIPLEThe formula is sovereign. The implementation is subordinate. The operational interpretation never replaces the formal core.

METHODOLOGY AT THE END OF THE LEARNING JOURNEY

DIIIP: how communication becomes data, intelligence and useful decisions

The same evidence chain connects our 11 C-Level responsibilities, the marketplace systems and the Don Espadín case. DIIIP is a teaching and audit framework—not a replacement for the official KAI·ROI v1 formula.

D
Data

Permissioned records of messages, products, customers, resources, orders, tasks, delivery and satisfaction.

I
Information

Records are organised into identifiers, cohorts, invoices, SKUs, SLA evidence, cost centres and accountable business processes.

I
Intelligence

Rules, analysis and AI interpret information to support decisions in demand, risk, operations, quality and customer relationships.

I
Insights

Executives detect conversion gaps, costs, capacity constraints, customer experience and opportunities to improve retention.

P
Personalization Actions

Evidence triggers relevant offers, service responses, workflow actions, learning improvements and responsible executive decisions.

KAI·ROI EQUATION · CUSTOMER EQUITY

From teaching evidence to measurable organisational value

This academy resource connects direction, customer data, AI, people, productivity, revenue, efficiency and portfolio health. The 19-month sprint and the Don Espadín exercises belong to the operational teaching layer.

The formal KAI·ROI v1 architecture remains sovereign. Operational indices, training examples and simulated figures never replace its official factors, Data Monetisation or Customer Equity calculation.
